chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abī ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about a eunuch who married a woman while she knew that he was a eunuch. He said: “It is permissible.”

It was said to him: “He remained with her for as long as Allah willed, then divorced her. Is there a waiting period upon her?” He said: “Yes. Has he not taken pleasure from her, and has she not taken pleasure from him?”
It was said to him: “Then is ghusl upon her regarding what occurs from her and from him?” He said: “If, when that occurred from him, she emitted sexual fluid, then ghusl is upon her.”
It was said to him: “Does he have the right to take back anything from the dowry if he divorces her?” He said: “No.”

key_terms.أَمْنَتْ: she emitted sexual fluid; experienced discharge triggering ghusl in this context
key_terms.تَزَوَّجَ: married; entered into a valid marriage contract
key_terms.خَصِيٍّ: a eunuch; a castrated man discussed here as a legal subject in marriage
key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: waiting period required of a woman after divorce
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required in certain states of sexual impurity
key_terms.ٱلصَّدَاقِ: the dowry given to the wife in marriage

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on marriage, ʿiddah, ghusl, and dowry when a woman marries a eunuch knowingly?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the marriage of a eunuch when the woman knowingly marries him. It affirms the validity of the marriage, establishes the waiting period after divorce due to mutual enjoyment, requires ghusl if sexual discharge occurs, and denies the husband any right to reclaim part of the dowry after divorce.
